messages.body:
Wren,

We got the CMF money. Slow Rooms is going ahead: seven months inside Oakmount Manor in Bedford, east wing, starting the first week of March. I want you for sound. Not because you're cheap (you're not, anymore) but because you're the only mixer I know who will sit in a corridor for four hours to get a room right and not complain about it.

The brief is: interviews with residents and staff, observational days, and a proper ambience library of the building at every hour. The library is yours to sell afterward; we just need the master.

Colin will send the numbers. Say yes.

N.

yes.

two things: I want the consent process to be real, not a form on a clipboard, especially for residents with dementia. and I want a night pass so I can record the building empty.

w

Both fine. Consent process is being reviewed by Oakmount's ethics person and by Paul Kavanagh (retired RCMP, our consultant on anything that might get us sued). Night access is approved for Tues/Thurs after 10pm with a staff escort for the first month, then on your own.

Contract attached. Day rate $650, 62 days guaranteed, plus $4,000 buyout on the ambience master. Kit rental on top.

Colin

threads.subject: Consent protocol — residents with cognitive impairment

messages.body:
Good afternoon,

Attached is the consent protocol our Resident Care Committee approved for the production. The key points:

1. Substitute decision-makers (SDMs) must sign for any resident who does not have capacity for this decision. Capacity is assessed per-decision by our nursing staff, not assumed from diagnosis.
2. Ongoing assent: if a resident indicates at any time that they do not want to be recorded, recording stops, regardless of SDM consent.
3. Recordings of residents are not to be shared with family members or third parties by the production without the SDM's written request and the Manor's review.

For Mr. Furey (Rm 17), the SDM is his son, Derek Furey. Consent form attached, signed.

Deborah Whynot, RN
Director of Resident Care, Oakmount Manor

Thank you, Deborah. Point 2 is the one I care most about and I'll follow it to the letter. I'll also keep a session log for every resident recording: who was present, how they seemed, whether they asked to stop.

Wren

Nadia,

Logs attached for the week. Most of it is what you'd expect. Two flags:

- 2026-05-12 Rm 22 (Mrs. Beazley): asked to stop at 14 min, we stopped. She was fine after, wanted tea.
- 2026-05-14 Rm 17 (Alden): I need to talk to you about this one in person. Not a consent issue exactly. Please don't open AF_03 until we've spoken. I mean that.

w
Understood. Monday, first thing. Don't send it anywhere.

Summary of this morning so we all have the same memory of it.

Present: Nadia, Wren, Colin, Paul (by phone).

1. Wren played the section of AF_03 from 40:30 to 44:10. Nobody spoke for a while afterward.
2. Paul's view: what Alden describes is consistent with the 1971 Mahar file as far as he knows it (he was not on that file; it predates him). It is also the statement of a man with a dementia diagnosis, made to a sound recordist he may have mistaken for someone else, during a film shoot. On its own it is not a case. It may be enough for HRP's historical unit to re-open and look for corroboration (Doucette's family, the vehicle, the Arm).
3. We do not use it in the film. Not now. Possibly not ever. That is Nadia's call and she has made it.
4. We do not tell the family (Derek Furey) at this stage. Paul's advice: telling the family before police is how evidence disappears.
5. Chain of custody: the original card stays in the Harbourlight safe. Wren keeps her working copy on an encrypted drive. No cloud. Wren will transcribe it herself, not with a service.
6. Paul will make an informal inquiry with a contact at HRP before anything formal, to see whether anyone is still alive to talk to.

Wren, thank you for handling this the way you did. Most people would have posted it.

Colin

That is an accurate account. One addition for Wren specifically: if Mr. Furey speaks about this again, let him. Do not prompt, do not ask questions, do not correct him. If he asks who you are, tell him the truth. Anything he says unprompted is worth ten times what he says when asked.

Regards,
Paul Kavanagh

understood. he hasn't mentioned it since. he asked me yesterday if the tide was in.

w

threads.subject: East wing corridor — ceiling and duct work July 13–18

messages.body:
Heads up that facilities will be replacing the corridor ceiling tiles and the return duct outside rooms 15–19 from July 13 to 18. Noise during the day; the crew will not work after 4pm. Residents in 17 and 18 will be moved to the day room during work hours.

Wren, I know you've been chasing the noise in that corridor. Facilities found a section of return duct with a failed hanger; it had dropped and was sitting on the tile grid. They think that's your hum. Mystery solved, I hope.

Deborah

That would do it. Thanks Deborah. Could I get one more night in the corridor before the 13th? I'd like a clean 'before'.

Wren
Thursday the 9th is fine. Sign in at the desk as usual.

I'm sorry to let you know that Mr. Alden Furey passed away in his sleep early this morning. His son has been notified and is on his way. We'd ask that the crew not be in the east wing today.

He liked having you around, Wren. He called you 'the girl with the fishing rod'. I think he meant the boom.

Deborah

as discussed. I replied once before you told me not to; my reply is below his. sorry.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Derek Furey <derek@fureymarine.ca>
Date: Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM
Subject: Recordings of my father

Ms. Castellanos,

I understand from the staff at Oakmount that you recorded a number of conversations with my late father during the production of the documentary. As his son and substitute decision-maker I would like copies of all such recordings for the family, and I would ask that the production delete its own copies once we have them. Dad was not himself in his last year and I don't think it's right for any of that to be out in the world.

I'm happy to come by and collect a drive.

Regards,
Derek Furey
President, Furey Marine Services Ltd.
902-468-3300

---
My reply, Aug 3 8:40 PM:

Mr. Furey,

I'm sorry for your loss. Your father was very kind to me.

The recordings belong to the production, not to me, so I've passed your request to Harbourlight's producer, Colin Tremblay, who will be in touch. I'd add that the consent your father's care team and you signed doesn't provide for copies to go to family, and that the recordings are covered by the film's participant agreement. I know that's not the answer you wanted.

Wren Castellanos

August invoice attached. 9 days + the AMB_MASTER delivery. The kit rental line is shorter than usual because I don't have the MixPre anymore, as you know.

w

Approved, paid Friday. And I've added $900 for a replacement recorder under the production's insurance, don't argue.

C
